hero.headline: Your repository is already a CMS.
hero.body: Give marketers and writers an editor for the Markdown you already have. Every change is a pull request you review. Nothing goes live until you Publish. Developers keep the repo, the history and the deploy; the rest of the team gets drafts, previews and a Publish button.
hero.note: Free and open source. Runs on your machine. Content stays in your repo.
hero.shotAlt: Orso previewing a blog post on the draft site, with the agent panel open beside it.

logos.label: Works with your stack
logos.title: Works with the stack you already have
logos.body: Astro, Markdown and GitHub for the site. Claude, Cursor, Codex or OpenCode for the agent — with the account and plan you already pay for. Orso adds no AI usage charges.

setup.title: Cost and setup
setup.body: Orso is free and open source. Connect your own AI coding agent and use your existing account and plan. You pay the agent provider directly; Orso adds no AI usage charges.
setup.detail: Install on your machine, open a repo, and your Markdown collections show up. There is nothing to migrate and no content database to leave behind. Teammates get drafts, previews and Publish; developers keep the same Git history and deploy path.

proof.eyebrow: Delete the CMS. Keep the editors.
proof.quote: “With AI and coding agents, the cost of an abstraction has never been higher.”
proof.note: That move works when everyone editing the site already works like a developer. Most marketing teams don't. Orso gives them forms, drafts and a Publish button — while the content stays in your repo. If it isn't simple enough for my own non-technical teammates, it isn't done.

faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.intro: Anything else, write to the team. A person replies, not a ticket bot. The {link} has step-by-step guides.

who.question: Who is Project Orso for?
who.answer: Teams where developers own the repo but marketers, writers and founders own the words. It gives the second group the tools the first already uses — drafts, previews, reviews and a coding agent — without asking them to learn any of it.

git.question: Does my team need to know Git or code?
git.answer: No. Copy, posts and help articles have forms, and anything bigger can go to the agent in plain English. They see drafts, previews and a Publish button, never branches or commits.

github.question: Does everyone need a GitHub account?
github.answer: Yes, and that's the only GitHub they'll touch. Access is your GitHub team, so there's no second login to manage and no separate list of who can publish.

migrate.question: Do I have to migrate my content?
migrate.answer: No. Orso reads the Markdown already in your repo. Open the repo and your posts and docs show up as collections.

sites.question: Which sites does it work with, and what does it add to my repo?
sites.answer: Astro 7 sites with a main branch. New sites start from Orso's template. For an existing site, Orso adds a small integration and loads your collections through it. A setup skill makes those changes on a branch for you to review.

live.question: Who decides what goes live?
live.answer: You do, through GitHub. Every change is a pull request into main, and Publish merges it once it's approved. Turn on branch protection and nothing merges without a review.

cms.question: How is this different from a hosted or Git-based CMS?
cms.answer: A hosted CMS keeps your content in its own database. A Git-based CMS keeps it in your repo and gives editors forms for the fields you configure. Orso also keeps it in your repo, then adds live previews of the real site, pull-request review and a coding agent for changes a form can't make.

break.question: Can someone break the live site?
break.answer: Not by accident. Every change lands in a draft with its own preview, nothing goes live until someone hits Publish, and every save is a checkpoint you can roll back in one click.

agent.question: Which AI agent do I need?
agent.answer: Claude, Cursor, Codex or OpenCode. If your team already pays for one of the first three, that's everything Orso needs. OpenCode runs free models and needs no account.

free.question: How is this free?
free.answer: Project Orso is an open-source project, not a product with plans. Read it, fork it, run it locally — there's no paid tier and nothing behind a paywall.

stop.question: What happens if we stop using Orso?
stop.answer: Nothing changes. Your content was always Markdown in your own repo, every change is already in its history, and the site is plain static files.

cta.title: Ready for your team to run the site?
cta.body: Install Orso once and connect the repo. After that, your team edits with drafts, previews and Publish.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.body: Give teammates a GitHub account, access to the repo, and an agent seat you already subscribe to. They edit real pages and write content in real Markdown — the same proven workflow developers have used forever. Publish is still a human decision.

edit.title: Edit the Markdown in your repo
edit.body: Forms and rich text for the posts, pages and docs already in your repo. Editors never have to open a code editor for day-to-day copy.

editor.demoTitle: A fresh start for our website
demoBody: We're rebuilding the marketing site around the content we already keep in Git — posts, pages and docs in Markdown.
Editors get forms and a live preview. Every save is a commit on a draft branch, and nothing goes live until someone clicks Publish.

preview.title: Preview the change on a branch
preview.body: Each edit is a draft branch with a live preview of the real site — desktop and phone — so you see the page as visitors will.

agent.title: Ask the agent for bigger changes
agent.body: Ask for a page, a section or a layout change in plain English. The agent edits the files; you still review the draft and own Publish.

publish.title: Review the draft, then Publish
publish.body: Compare the draft against live, keep or undo changes, and Publish when you are ready. Nothing merges until someone decides.

git.title: Stays in Git
git.body: Your content is Markdown in your repo — not a proprietary database. Every save is a commit with a real author, a message and a history you can roll back.

branches.title: Draft branches
branches.body: Each change lands on its own draft branch with a live preview. Review the page, then Publish to merge into main. Branch protection still applies.

stack.title: Your stack
stack.body: Astro for the site, Markdown for the words, GitHub for review and deploy. Orso does not replace your host or ask you to move the content elsewhere.
